title: The Ellipse: Two Foci and a String

steps.body: An **ellipse** is every point whose distances to **two fixed foci** add up to a constant. Pin a string at both foci, pull it taut with a pencil, and trace: the constant string length is the sum. That sum equals **2a**, the length of the long (major) axis.

widget.prompt: Slide the eccentricity to 0.6 and watch the two focal distances as the point travels — their SUM is what to keep an eye on.
widget.successFeedback: The two distances trade off but always total the same 2a. That constant sum is the ellipse's definition — the pin-and-string construction — and the eccentricity only decides how far apart the pins sit.
widget.explorationFeedback: Slide a few more times. The claim is that the sum is constant for EVERY position, which one snapshot cannot establish.

explanationVariants: At the vertex (5, 0) with foci (±4, 0): distances 1 and 9 sum to 10 = 2a. The definition holds.
1 + 9 = 10 confirms the constant sum at the far end of the major axis.

widget.prompt: Foci at (±4, 0), vertex at (5, 0). The distances to the two foci are 1 and 9. What is their sum?

commonErrors.feedback: 8 = 9 − 1 subtracts. The ellipse uses the SUM: 1 + 9 = 10.
4 is the focal distance c. Add the two distances: 1 + 9 = 10.

steps.body:
Centered at the origin, the ellipse has the tidy equation

x²/a² + y²/b² = 1,

with **a > b**. Here a is the semi-major axis (half the long way) and b the semi-minor (half the short way). For x²/25 + y²/9 = 1: a = 5, b = 3 — the curve reaches 5 along x and 3 along y.

explanationVariants: x²/25 + y²/9 = 1: a = √25 = 5 (semi-major, along x) and b = √9 = 3 (semi-minor).
The denominators are a² and b²: take square roots to get 5 and 3.

widget.prompt: For x²/25 + y²/9 = 1, what is the semi-major axis length a?

commonErrors.feedback: 25 is a², not a. Take the square root: a = √25 = 5.

explanationVariants: The larger denominator sits under x² (25 > 9), so the major axis is horizontal — the ellipse is wider than it is tall.
a² = 25 is under x², so the long axis runs along x.

widget.prompt: For x²/25 + y²/9 = 1, the major (long) axis is:

options.label: horizontal (along the x-axis)
options.feedback: Right — the bigger denominator (25) is under x², so the ellipse stretches horizontally.

options.label: vertical (along the y-axis)
options.feedback: The larger denominator is under x² here, so the long axis is HORIZONTAL.

options.label: diagonal
options.feedback: Axis-aligned ellipses stretch along x or y. Here the bigger denominator (25) is under x²: horizontal.

explanationVariants: x²/9 + y²/25 = 1 now has the 25 under y², so a = 5 along the VERTICAL axis; 2a = 10.
When the larger denominator is under y², the major axis is vertical with a = 5, giving 2a = 10.

widget.prompt: For x²/9 + y²/25 = 1, what is the major axis length 2a?

commonErrors.feedback: 6 = 2·3 uses the smaller value. a = √25 = 5, so 2a = 10.
5 = a. The full major axis is 2a = 10.

takeaways: Ellipse = points whose distances to two foci sum to 2a.
Standard form x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 with a > b.
The larger denominator marks the major (long) axis direction.
steps.teaser: Next: locating the foci from a and b.

concept.body: Ellipse: distances to two foci sum to 2a. Standard form x²/a²+y²/b²=1 with a>b; the larger denominator is a² and marks the major axis.

widget.prompt: For x²/16 + y²/4 = 1, what is a (the semi-major axis)?

commonErrors.feedback: 16 is a². Take the root: a = 4.
